UP CM Yogi Adityanath Calls for Review of Electoral Rolls Following Claims of Missing Voters

Overview of Electoral Roll Claims

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) workers to conduct a detailed review of electoral rolls at the booth level. The Chief Minister claims that a significant number of potential voters are currently absent from the state's official electoral lists.

Breakdown of Reported Figures

During a BJP state working committee meeting, Adityanath presented statistics suggesting that approximately 1.27 crore individuals are not registered as voters. His claims include:

  • Panchayat Roll Discrepancy: Roughly 66 lakh individuals listed in panchayat electoral rolls are reportedly missing from Assembly constituency voter lists.
  • Welfare Scheme Beneficiaries: Approximately 55 lakh recipients of state government welfare schemes are allegedly unregistered.
  • Young Voters: About 4.5 lakh individuals aged 18-19 are reportedly missing from the rolls.

Official Context and ECI Data

While the Chief Minister maintains that the state's voter count should exceed 16 crore based on population estimates, current official data presents a different figure. According to the Election Commission of India (ECI), the final electorate for Uttar Pradesh stands at approximately 13.39 crore following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The ECI data indicates that while over 84 lakh new voters were added, more than 2.04 crore voters were removed, with a notable concentration of deletions in urban areas.

Call to Action

Adityanath has tasked party MPs, MLAs, and local office-bearers with overseeing the verification process. BJP workers are being encouraged to:

  • Coordinate with Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to facilitate registrations.
  • Conduct regular reviews of voter lists at every polling booth.
  • Encourage members of the public to verify their own registration status via official ECI channels.

Citizens are advised to visit the official Election Commission of India website or the Voter Service Portal to confirm their enrollment status independently of any political campaigns.
